basis: Isolated sperm flagellar defects and male infertility affect reproductive function; no supported extra-reproductive involvement.
Chemotherapy-induced inflammation and ulceration of oral mucosa; mouth belongs to gastrointestinal.
Benign blood vessel neoplasm arising in the orbit.
Benign ovarian neoplasm; reproductive site without defining endocrine dysfunction.
Brain neoplasm arising in the pineal gland, an endocrine gland.
Spastic paraplegia and Paget bone disease define the syndrome; skeletal abnormalities and fractures occur in 80-99%.
Malignant vascular endothelial neoplasm; anatomical sites vary across the umbrella, so no additional site applies consistently.
Gallbladder wall inflammation; gallbladder belongs to hepatic. Inflammation alone does not establish an immune-mediated mechanism.
Benign vascular neoplasm arising in the spleen; splenic and blood vessel origin are both defined.
Trabecular pigment deposition causes raised intraocular pressure and glaucomatous optic nerve damage within the eye.
Carcinoma originates in breast; apocrine differentiation does not establish a skin primary.
Site-unspecified treatment-resistant cancer; no organ axis can be assigned across all possible primary sites.
Persistent common urethral and vaginal channel includes a structural abnormality of the urinary outlet; reproductive involvement has no axis.
Bilateral congenital fusion of humerus, radius and ulna defines a skeletal disorder.
Primary glial brain neoplasm; IDH mutation is a tumor marker and does not establish a systemic metabolic disorder.
Fibromuscular dysplasia directly affects extremity arterial walls; the name does not imply skeletal muscle disease.
Megakaryoblastic leukemia affects marrow and blood; hepatic infiltration with hepatomegaly is usual (>30%). Splenic involvement shares the haematologic axis.
Inherited melanin metabolism disorder defined by ocular and cutaneous hypopigmentation, with characteristic visual dysfunction.
Dystonia combined with another neurological movement disorder; abnormal muscle contractions do not establish primary muscle disease.
Ocular strain associated with refractive or ocular alignment problems; headache does not establish neurological damage.
Severe protein-energy deficiency; direct skeletal muscle catabolism and wasting occur in nearly all patients.
Vibrio infection of intestine; dehydration and electrolyte changes are acute consequences. Kidney injury occurs in only 5-29% and is separately diagnosed.
Secondary glaucoma causes intraocular pressure elevation and optic nerve damage; systemic deposits do not establish other organ damage.
Nonsyndromic X-linked intellectual disability with delayed speech and language development.
Autoimmune enteropathy with obligatory villous atrophy. Anemia and dermatitis are separate diagnoses; frequent transaminase elevation alone does not prove liver damage.
